anomalies.observed: On the bottom bus connector J2 the +3V3 wire lands on pin 11 (the row labelled PIN11, i.e. the 3.3 V pin of the M-BUS legend), but on the top connector J1 the +3V3 wire is drawn two rows higher, landing on pin 7 (the row labelled PIN7 / G25 in the M-BUS legend), while J1 pin 11 carries only a PWR_FLAG marker. The two connectors therefore do not present the same net on the same pin number.
anomalies.expected: The specification states J1 and J2 carry 'identical nets on both so the board can be stacked ... Carries +5V, +3V3, BAT, GND, GPIO/UART pins'. +3V3 must be wired to the same pin (pin 11) on both J1 and J2, and the GPIO pin 7 must not be tied to a supply rail.

evidence.quote: J2 left column: '+3V3' arrow connected at the PIN11 row; J1 left column: '+3V3' arrow connected at the PIN7 row, PWR_FLAG at PIN11 (root sheet, columns 1-2)
J1 / J2 ... identical nets on both so the board can be stacked between the M5Stack Core and a lower module (pass-through). Carries +5V, +3V3, BAT, GND, GPIO/UART pins

anomalies.impact: The 3.3 V rail is shorted onto the pin-7 GPIO net on J1 (conflicting with the M5Stack Core's G25/DAC pin when the Core is plugged in), and 3.3 V is not passed through to J2 pin 11, so any module stacked on the bottom connector loses its 3.3 V supply and receives 3.3 V on the wrong pin.

parsed.summary: All component values, parts, diode orientations, jumper-selectable PWM/serial paths and the power/switching circuitry match the specification, but the +3V3 rail is wired to a different pin on J1 (pin 7) than on J2 (pin 11), breaking the intended pass-through and shorting a GPIO pin to the 3.3 V supply on the top connector.
